findings.finding: The stack's cited source did not exist in the repository, so 103 tools, 12 licence exclusions and 7 must-build ports rested on a dangling claim. The owner supplied it mid-phase.
findings.evidence: Verified rather than assumed on arrival: 103 of 103 tool names are supported by the document, 4 of them through a declared name variant (OPA, Kafka, Kata, OTel Collector); all 12 excluded tools are named in its exclusion list, MinIO on line 392; the stack's 7 build-ports map onto the document's 6 must-build rows with layer 7 split in two. Both artifacts are dated 2026-09-11.
findings.found_by: author at ceremony 15; resolved by the owner
findings.suggested_change: Place it at the path the citation names so the claim is literally true, and gate on its existence so the dangling case cannot recur silently.

findings.finding: The first cut blocked on any tool absent from the cited document. That is the wrong direction: cellplane-stack.js is the maturer artifact -- it is what the page renders and what the extractor derives from -- and the markdown is its stated source, which may lag. Blocking there would force a newly chosen tool to wait for prose to catch up.
findings.evidence: Owner's note mid-phase: the .js 'might be more mature though'.
findings.suggested_change: Block only on the document being absent. Report tools ahead of the source by name, never blocking, so divergence is visible without being an obstacle.

findings.finding: First run flagged examples/end-to-end as having no grader. It is not an area: examples/reference/README.md states outright that it 'is the reference walk across all of them, not one of them'. Discovery had copied examples_gate.py's globs, which answer a different question -- what is gated, not what is an area.
findings.evidence: grader_isolation first run: `BLOCK end-to-end missing no grader at end-to-end.sh`.
findings.found_by: the tool, on its first run
findings.suggested_change: Declare the exclusion in the tool with its citation. An undeclared exclusion is how a rule loses its corpus quietly.

findings.finding: The `invoked` plant did not fire: the temp tree flattened the grader path to hidden/ while the invoke pattern looks for night/hidden/, so the arm would have shipped proven by nothing. This is the third consecutive phase in which a planted defect failed to fire on the first attempt -- named_proof's plant was overwritten, inert_check's document arm had no live corpus, and now this.
findings.evidence: Self-test: `planted verdicts caught: ['inside', 'missing']`, with the assertion requiring all three by name and correctly printing FAIL.
findings.suggested_change: Mirror the real layout in the temp tree. More generally: a plant that does not fire is the normal case on first write, which is the argument for asserting each verdict BY NAME rather than 'some finding'.

findings.finding: The core of this lesson cannot be decided by any check inside the repository. It says graders live outside the tree until grading; this repo's are committed at docs/night/hidden/ beside the areas they grade, so the separation rests on the author choosing not to look. That exposes a gap in the loop itself: a capability item's only stop condition is 'becomes a wired, self-tested tool', so a lesson whose control is procedural has nowhere to go but permanent debt or a no-op tool -- and the no-op route is what ceremony 13 caught.
findings.evidence: tools/improvement_loop.py capability_candidates(): the only exit is runs-and-is-self-tested.
findings.found_by: author, building the tool and finding the residue unmechanisable
findings.suggested_change: Close on the checkable part with the residue split out and named, as here. Separately, the loop needs an explicit `process` disposition with a named compensating control, counted apart and never silent -- recorded in lesson 16b-grader-out-of-tree.
